actions.title: Validate Local Milk Demand
actions.description: Confirm actual daily consumption potential with nearby sweet shops and retail vendors.
actions.whatToDo: Visit 5 local sweet shops and 10 retail grocery stores in a 5km radius to ask about their daily unadulterated milk requirements.
actions.expectedOutcome: A confirmed list of at least 3 initial bulk buyers.

reasons: Strong local preference for fresh dairy
Historical data on sweet shop density

why.summary: Securing bulk buyers early minimizes inventory wastage.
factors: High competition for retail shelf space

evidence.label: Sweet shops make up 40% of local bulk buys

actions.title: Compare Fodder Suppliers
actions.description: Identify and negotiate with suitable local cattle feed suppliers to reduce operational costs.
actions.whatToDo: Get quotes from 3 different wholesale fodder suppliers. Compare prices for dry fodder vs green fodder.
actions.expectedOutcome: A signed 3-month contract with the most cost-effective supplier.

actions.title: Arrange Initial Capital
actions.description: Secure funding for the first batch of 10 cows and basic shed infrastructure.
actions.whatToDo: Apply for the NABARD Dairy Entrepreneurship Development Scheme (DEDS). Prepare the required project report.

why.summary: NABARD schemes offer significant subsidies for rural dairy setups.

actions.title: Acquire Necessary Licenses
actions.description: Ensure all local panchayat and FSSAI registrations are completed.
actions.whatToDo: Submit application for basic FSSAI registration and obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Gram Panchayat.
actions.expectedOutcome: Legal clearance to operate and sell dairy products.
